original_question: Let F be the abelian group of algebraic functions with the Fermat property. Let D be the subgroup generated by logarithmic derivatives U^(partial)(x) = xU'(x) of algebraic functions U(x), let Z[x] be the polynomial subgroup, and let P be the subgroup generated by finite sums of power-substituted algebraic functions U_j(x^{M_j}) with M_j >= 2. For an algebraic function U over Q(x) that is unramified at x = 0, let F_U = F intersect Q(x, U), D_U = D intersect Q(x, U), and P_U = P intersect Q(x, U). Determine the structure of the quotient groups F/(D + Z[x] + P), A_U = F_U/(D_U + Z[x]), and P_U = F_U/(D_U + Z[x] + P_U). In particular, determine the corresponding quotient in the purely rational case Q(x).
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 2 of arXiv:1609.09842, the refinement of Problem 1 on algebraic functions with a Fermat property.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the quotient-group refinement of the Fermat-property problem rather than the broader initial classification problem. It keeps the ambient field Q(x), the unramified-at-0 hypothesis, the additive group F of algebraic functions with the Fermat property, the differential subgroup D coming from U^(partial)(x) = xU'(x), the polynomial subgroup Z[x], the power-substitution subgroup P, the field-restricted pieces F_U, D_U, P_U, and the special purely rational case.
missing_details: The paper first defines the Fermat property via a power series R(x) = sum_{n>=0} s(n)x^n in Z[[x]] that is algebraic over Q(x), unramified at x = 0, and satisfies s(p) = 0 mod p for all sufficiently large primes p; your draft should restate this explicitly.
The quantifier 'for all sufficiently large primes p' should be made explicit: there exists N such that for every prime p > N, the congruence holds.
The paper identifies algebraic functions with their Laurent expansions at x = 0; this should be stated to make the intersections F_U, D_U, P_U stand-alone.
In the definition of D, the paper motivates xU'(x) by noting that if U is algebraic then xU'(x) lies in the same algebraic function field Q(x,U); this is part of the intended scope.
In the definition of P, the source functions used before substitution x -> x^M are required to be algebraic, unramified at 0, and without a pole at 0, with M >= 2.
Your draft uses P_U both for the subgroup P intersect Q(x,U) and for a quotient; this notation clashes and should be corrected in the refined version.
The paper poses this as an open problem to 'find the structure' of the indicated abelian groups, not as an already proved classification theorem.
The specified paper is an open-problems note; the official label here is Problem 2, not Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3.
refined_question: Let R(x) = sum_{n>=0} s(n)x^n in Z[[x]] be an algebraic function over Q(x), unramified at x = 0, such that s(p) = 0 mod p for all sufficiently large primes p; call such an R an algebraic function with a Fermat property. Let F be the additive abelian group of all such functions. For any algebraic function U(x), define U^(partial)(x) = xU'(x), and let D be the subgroup of F generated by all such logarithmic derivatives; let Z[x] be the polynomial subgroup. If V(x) is algebraic over Q(x), unramified at 0 and without a pole at 0, and M >= 2 is an integer, let V(x^M) be a basic power-substituted element, and let P be the subgroup generated by finite sums of such elements. For any algebraic U over Q(x) that is unramified at 0, identify functions with their Laurent expansions at 0 and set F_U = F intersect Q(x,U), D_U = D intersect Q(x,U), and P_U = P intersect Q(x,U). Find the structure of the abelian quotient groups F/(D + Z[x] + P), F_U/(D_U + Z[x]), and F_U/(D_U + Z[x] + P_U). In particular, what is the corresponding quotient in the purely rational case Q(x)?
justification: In the specified paper, Section 1 first introduces the Fermat-property condition as Problem 1 and then immediately refines it by defining the additive group F, the subgroups D, Z[x], and P, and the restricted pieces F_U, D_U, and P_U before asking for the structure of the resulting quotients in Problem 2. That is exactly the mathematical content your draft is trying to encode. The main fixes needed are to restore the coefficientwise congruence definition of the Fermat property from Problem 1, make the Laurent-series identification at x = 0 explicit, retain the pole-free hypothesis in the definition of P, spell out the quantifier in 'for all sufficiently large primes', and avoid the notation clash in which P_U names both a subgroup and a quotient. Also, arXiv:1609.09842 is a short open-problems note: the nearest official formulation here is Problem 2 in Section 1.
